This report follows the structure of the VPAT® 2.5 (WCAG edition). It covers **Lumen 0.1.0** (web, desktop and mobile) against **WCAG 2.2** levels A and AA, and was last reviewed on **2026-11-14**. It is published again with every major release: `node scripts/acr.mjs --check` fails when the report's version and the app's differ.

## Summary

| Level | Supports | Partially supports | Does not support | Not applicable |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | 21 | 6 | 0 | 4 |
| AA | 15 | 7 | 0 | 2 |

## How it was evaluated

Automated: axe-core on six surfaces in Hebrew and English, light and dark (e2e/a11y.spec.ts); reflow at 320 and 640 px and forced colours (e2e/reflow.spec.ts); spoken announcements (e2e/sr-announce.spec.ts); unit tests of the focus trap, contrast and toasts. Manual: review of each criterion against the app's code and behaviour for this version. The automated part is generated from an axe-core run (docs/acr/axe.json, scripts/acr-axe.mjs): each criterion shows the axe rules that test it, and a criterion axe finds a violation of can't be reported as supported.

## Automated testing

**axe-core 4.11.3**, the app's components in headless Chromium, with the app's compiled CSS (offline harness), on 2026-11-14 (commit `ad415c29a3`): 159 runs on 53 surfaces × 3 setups (he/light, he/dark, en/light), 32 WCAG 2.0/2.1/2.2 A and AA rules, **4 rules with violations**. The "axe" column below shows, for each criterion, the rules that test it and how they came out. axe tests only part of WCAG; the rest is checked by hand, as described above.

Not tested this way (covered by the e2e suite): SearchDialog, HelpPanel.

## Level A

| Criterion | Status | Remarks | axe |
|---|---|---|---|
| [1.1.1 Non-text Content](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/non-text-content) | Partially supports | Icons and icon buttons have text names (axe). Charts, diagrams, the canvas and maps drawn from note text are pictures: their alternative is the source text in the note, which is always one click away, but the picture itself has no text alternative. **Plan:** Give chart and diagram blocks a text summary (title, series, values) as their accessible name, and the canvas an outline of its shapes. (0.2.0) | — (not testable by axe) |
| [1.2.1 Audio-only and Video-only (Prerecorded)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/audio-only-and-video-only-prerecorded) | Not applicable | Lumen's own interface has no prerecorded audio or video. Media in notes is the author's content. | — (not testable by axe) |
| [1.2.2 Captions (Prerecorded)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/captions-prerecorded) | Not applicable | No prerecorded media with sound in the interface. | — (not testable by axe) |
| [1.2.3 Audio Description or Media Alternative (Prerecorded)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/audio-description-or-media-alternative-prerecorded) | Not applicable | No prerecorded video in the interface. | — (not testable by axe) |
| [1.3.1 Info and Relationships](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/info-and-relationships) | Partially supports | Dialogs, menus, the palette (combobox + listbox), tabs, tables and forms use native elements or ARIA roles with names. In the editor, the structure of the line under the cursor (heading level, task state, code block, quote) is spoken. axe (W3.8 run) finds one exception: the calendar's month grid has grid cells and column headers without rows (aria-required-children/-parent, critical). **Plan:** Give the calendar grid real rows (role=row with display: contents) and the day button inside its cell — done in #522 (W6.30); the next axe run after it lands turns this back to supports. (0.2.0) | ✗ 6 violations: aria-required-children (CalendarPanel, he/light); aria-required-children (CalendarPanel, he/dark); aria-required-children (CalendarPanel, en/light); aria-required-parent (CalendarPanel, he/light) |
| [1.3.2 Meaningful Sequence](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/meaningful-sequence) | Supports | The reading order follows the DOM order in both directions; Hebrew and English runs are isolated so they read in their own direction. | — (not testable by axe) |
| [1.3.3 Sensory Characteristics](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/sensory-characteristics) | Supports | Instructions name the control ("the Settings button", "⌘K"), never only its shape, colour or place. | — (not testable by axe) |
| [1.4.1 Use of Color](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/use-of-color) | Partially supports | Messages, errors and selections carry text or a named icon as well as colour (axe's colour rules pass on six surfaces). In the status bar, the sync and collaboration indicators show their state by icon and colour, with the words only in a tooltip. **Plan:** Status-bar indicators with a visible word ("Synced", "Offline") and an accessible name, translated (their tooltips are English-only today). (0.2.0) | ✓ 1 rule, 12 checks passed |
| [1.4.2 Audio Control](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/audio-control) | Supports | Nothing plays sound on its own. Read-aloud starts on request and has a stop control. | — (not testable by axe) |
| [2.1.1 Keyboard](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/keyboard) | Partially supports | Every feature is a command in the palette, dialogs keep and return focus, the sidebar edge resizes with arrow keys. The canvas whiteboard (tldraw) and the map can be panned and zoomed with the keyboard, but drawing new shapes needs a pointer. **Plan:** Keyboard commands to add, move and connect shapes on the canvas. (0.2.0) | ✓ 1 rule, 20 checks passed |
| [2.1.2 No Keyboard Trap](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/no-keyboard-trap) | Supports | Tab in the editor indents (as in every code editor); pressing Escape and then Tab moves focus out (CodeMirror's behaviour). Dialogs release focus on Escape. | — (not testable by axe) |
| [2.1.4 Character Key Shortcuts](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/character-key-shortcuts) | Supports | Global shortcuts use a modifier (⌘ / Ctrl / Alt). Single-key keys work only while a component has focus (lists, the calendar grid), or in Vim mode, which is off unless turned on. | — (not testable by axe) |

Notifications that go away on their own stay while the pointer is over them or focus is in them (fixed for this report), and every one has a close button. | — (not testable by axe) |
| [2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/pause-stop-hide) | Supports | No content moves or blinks for more than five seconds, except progress spinners while work runs. With the system's reduce-motion setting, animations stop. | — (not testable by axe) |
| [2.3.1 Three Flashes or Below Threshold](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/three-flashes-or-below-threshold) | Supports | Nothing flashes. | — (not testable by axe) |
| [2.4.1 Bypass Blocks](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/bypass-blocks) | Supports | A skip link jumps to the main content; landmarks name the regions. | — (not testable by axe) |

| [2.4.3 Focus Order](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/focus-order) | Supports | Focus moves in reading order; a dialog takes focus when it opens and gives it back when it closes. | — (not testable by axe) |
| [2.4.4 Link Purpose (In Context)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/link-purpose-in-context) | Supports | Interface links say where they go; "Learn more" links sit inside the message they belong to. | ✓ 1 rule, 20 checks passed |
| [2.5.1 Pointer Gestures](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/pointer-gestures) | Supports | Nothing needs a multi-point or path gesture: pinch-zoom on the canvas, the map and the graph also has buttons, the wheel or keys. | — (not testable by axe) |

| [2.5.4 Motion Actuation](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/motion-actuation) | Not applicable | No feature uses device motion. | — (not testable by axe) |

| [3.2.1 On Focus](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/on-focus) | Supports | Focusing a control never changes the context. | — (not testable by axe) |

| [3.3.1 Error Identification](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/error-identification) | Supports | Errors are written in text next to the field, with role="alert" (for example an invalid daily-note pattern, a bad theme file, a failed sign-in). | — (not testable by axe) |

The canvas and the map are third-party widgets with partial roles. **Plan:** Extend the axe run to every panel and dialog, and wrap the canvas and the map in labelled regions with a keyboard summary. (0.2.0) | ✓ 18 rules, 1,528 checks passed |

| Criterion | Status | Remarks | axe |
|---|---|---|---|
| [1.2.4 Captions (Live)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/captions-live) | Not applicable | No live audio or video in the interface (collaboration is text only). | — (not testable by axe) |

| [1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/contrast-minimum) | Partially supports | Body text, controls and the built-in themes meet 4.5:1 in light and dark mode. axe (W3.8 run) finds status text below it: the status bar's privacy badge, the version history's storage warning, an onboarding and a collaboration note in dark mode (11 results on 5 surfaces), all coloured with the --success/--warning fill tokens (3.0–3.6:1). **Plan:** Colour status text with the text tokens --ok/--warn (≥ 4.5:1) instead of the fill tokens — done in #522 (W6.30); re-run axe after it lands. (0.2.0) | ✗ 11 violations: color-contrast (StatusBar, he/light); color-contrast (StatusBar, en/light); color-contrast (OnboardingTour, he/dark); color-contrast (CollabSettings, he/dark) |

| [1.4.5 Images of Text](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/images-of-text) | Supports | The interface uses real text, never pictures of text. | — (not testable by axe) |
| [1.4.10 Reflow](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/reflow) | Supports | At 320 CSS px wide (400 % zoom) the main screen, side panels and dialogs fit without horizontal scrolling. Code blocks and tables scroll inside their own box (allowed for two-dimensional content). | — (not testable by axe) |
| [1.4.11 Non-text Contrast](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/non-text-contrast) | Partially supports | Focus rings, the accent and icons meet 3:1. In the default theme the borders of some text fields are lighter than 3:1 against the background; the High contrast theme meets it everywhere. **Plan:** Darken input borders (--border-strong for fields) to 3:1 in every theme, and add the check to the contrast report. (0.2.0) | — (not testable by axe) |
| [1.4.12 Text Spacing](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/text-spacing) | Partially supports | Layouts use flexible boxes and should take the WCAG text-spacing overrides, but this has not been tested automatically yet. **Plan:** An e2e that applies the WCAG text-spacing styles to ten surfaces and checks nothing is cut off. (0.2.0) | ✓ 1 rule, 144 checks passed |
| [1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/content-on-hover-or-focus) | Partially supports | Tooltips are mostly the browser's own (title). Link previews and some popovers appear on hover; not all can be dismissed with Escape without moving the pointer. **Plan:** One popover component: dismissible with Escape, hoverable, persistent until dismissed. (0.2.0) | — (not testable by axe) |
| [2.4.5 Multiple Ways](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/multiple-ways) | Supports | Notes can be reached from the file tree, search, the command palette (quick open), backlinks, tags and the graph. | — (not testable by axe) |
| [2.4.6 Headings and Labels](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/headings-and-labels) | Supports | Dialogs and panels have headings; fields have labels that say what they are for. | — (not testable by axe) |
| [2.4.7 Focus Visible](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/focus-visible) | Supports | Every focusable element shows a focus ring, also in forced-colours mode. | — (not testable by axe) |

Notifications in the corner can sit over a focused control near the bottom edge until they go away. **Plan:** Move notifications away from the focused element, and an e2e that tabs through the main screen with notifications showing. (0.2.0) | — (not testable by axe) |
| [2.5.7 Dragging Movements](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/dragging-movements) | Partially supports | Reordering document tabs is by dragging only; there is no single-pointer or command alternative yet. Resizing the sidebar by its edge has a keyboard alternative, but not a single-pointer one. **Plan:** "Move tab left / right" in the tab's menu and the palette, and a width menu on the sidebar edge. (0.2.0) | — (not testable by axe) |
| [2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/target-size-minimum) | Partially supports | Most controls are 24×24 CSS px or larger, or spaced so a 24 px circle fits. A few icon buttons in dense panels (the calendar's arrows, a toast's close button) are smaller. axe (W3.8 run) confirms: 13 results on DocTabs' close buttons, the vault-encryption dialog's close, the calendar header and the usability panel. **Plan:** Enlarge those buttons to 24 px — done in #522 (W6.30) — and keep the axe target-size rule in the run. (0.2.0) | ✗ 13 violations: target-size (DocTabs, en/light); target-size (VaultEncryptionDialog, he/light); target-size (CalendarPanel, he/light); target-size (VaultEncryptionDialog, he/dark) |

| [3.2.3 Consistent Navigation](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/consistent-navigation) | Supports | The title bar, sidebar, status bar and palette are in the same place on every screen. | — (not testable by axe) |
| [3.2.4 Consistent Identification](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/consistent-identification) | Supports | The same function has the same name and icon everywhere (commands, menus and buttons share their strings). | — (not testable by axe) |
| [3.3.3 Error Suggestion](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/error-suggestion) | Supports | Error messages say how to fix the problem ("The pattern must contain YYYY, MM and DD"). | — (not testable by axe) |

| [4.1.3 Status Messages](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/status-messages) | Supports | Notifications are in live regions that are always on the page (role="status", errors role="alert"; fixed for this report), and the editor speaks its own changes through the shared live regions. | — (not testable by axe) |

## Exceptions and remediation plan

Every criterion not fully supported, and what will be done about it:

- **1.1.1 Non-text Content** (A, Partially supports): Give chart and diagram blocks a text summary (title, series, values) as their accessible name, and the canvas an outline of its shapes. Target: 0.2.0.
- **1.3.1 Info and Relationships** (A, Partially supports): Give the calendar grid real rows (role=row with display: contents) and the day button inside its cell — done in #522 (W6.30); the next axe run after it lands turns this back to supports. Target: 0.2.0.
- **1.4.1 Use of Color** (A, Partially supports): Status-bar indicators with a visible word ("Synced", "Offline") and an accessible name, translated (their tooltips are English-only today). Target: 0.2.0.
- **2.1.1 Keyboard** (A, Partially supports): Keyboard commands to add, move and connect shapes on the canvas. Target: 0.2.0.
- **2.4.2 Page Titled** (A, Supports): Show the open note's name in the page title. Target: 0.2.0.
- **2.5.3 Label in Name** (A, Partially supports): A manual pass over every toolbar and dialog, recorded in the screen reader protocol. Target: 0.2.0.
- **4.1.2 Name, Role, Value** (A, Partially supports): Extend the axe run to every panel and dialog, and wrap the canvas and the map in labelled regions with a keyboard summary. Target: 0.2.0.
- **1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum)** (AA, Partially supports): Colour status text with the text tokens --ok/--warn (≥ 4.5:1) instead of the fill tokens — done in #522 (W6.30); re-run axe after it lands. Target: 0.2.0.
- **1.4.11 Non-text Contrast** (AA, Partially supports): Darken input borders (--border-strong for fields) to 3:1 in every theme, and add the check to the contrast report. Target: 0.2.0.
- **1.4.12 Text Spacing** (AA, Partially supports): An e2e that applies the WCAG text-spacing styles to ten surfaces and checks nothing is cut off. Target: 0.2.0.
- **1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus** (AA, Partially supports): One popover component: dismissible with Escape, hoverable, persistent until dismissed. Target: 0.2.0.
- **2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum)** (AA, Partially supports): Move notifications away from the focused element, and an e2e that tabs through the main screen with notifications showing. Target: 0.2.0.
- **2.5.7 Dragging Movements** (AA, Partially supports): "Move tab left / right" in the tab's menu and the palette, and a width menu on the sidebar edge. Target: 0.2.0.
- **2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum)** (AA, Partially supports): Enlarge those buttons to 24 px — done in #522 (W6.30) — and keep the axe target-size rule in the run. Target: 0.2.0.

## Removed in WCAG 2.2

- 4.1.1 Parsing: Removed in WCAG 2.2 (always satisfied for HTML).

## Accessibility contact

Hit a barrier? Open an [accessibility report](https://github.com/talstilkol/lumen-md/issues/new?template=accessibility.yml) (a form labelled **accessibility**), or choose **Report an accessibility problem** in the command palette. Accessibility reports are triaged before other bugs. See also the [accessibility statement](/editor/accessibility-statement/).
